title: Privilege-caging: RBAC v2 temporal throttles and KMS consumption sandbox
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a privilege-caging middleware that enforces temporal operator throttles, per-operator KMS consumption sandboxing, and enhanced audit context enrichment. Backwards-compatible; feature gated behind 'privilege_caging' feature flag for rollout.
body:
Summary: Adds a 'privilege-cage' enforcement layer to RBAC v2 which can enforce short-term throttles on high-privilege operator roles, route KMS calls through a consumption sandbox adapter for accounting and safe-failover, and enrich audit events with consumption buckets and dry-run indicators. Motivation: incidents over the last quarter showed operators and automation agents consuming disproportionate KMS quotas during emergency flows, increasing latency and SLO risk. This PR gives platform teams a way to cap and observe operator-level KMS consumption, run dry-runs, and progressively enforce via feature flag.

Design highlights: privilege_cage middleware (services/authz) inspects RBAC v2 decision, looks up temporal throttles from policy cache, and either allows, rate-limits, or short-circuits requests. KMS sandbox adapter (infra/kms) is an in-process proxy that annotates requests with a sandbox-id, enforces per-operator consumption budgets, and can route to a safe-fallback KMS provider on budget exhaustion. Audit fanout sanitizer records pre/post consumption estimates, bucket labels, and whether the request was enforcement or dry-run. All persisted as structured audit fields for downstream compliance pipelines.

Rollout plan: gated behind 'privilege_caging' feature flag. Step 1: enable read-only dry-run globally to populate telemetry (two weeks). Step 2: soft-enforce for a small subset of tenants (canary) and monitor alarms. Step 3: full enforcement for operator roles after OK from compliance and SRE.

Checklist:
- [x] Middleware implementation and unit tests
- [x] KMS sandbox adapter and integration tests with mock KMS
- [x] Audit enrichment and retention config updates
- [x] Feature flag + config schema migration
- [x] Documentation and runbook for on-call (docs/security/privilege-caging.md)

Testing: added end-to-end integration harness exercising per-operator budget exhaustion, fallback routing, and audit emission. Load tests simulating operator spikes were run in benchmark-lab with observed KMS consumption isolation and <3% end-to-end latency impact under typical traffic.

Backward compatibility and migration: policy cache schema extended with optional TemporalThrottle metadata. If absent, legacy behavior is unchanged. KMS sandbox adapter exposes a pass-through mode when the 'sandbox_mode' config is off.

Security considerations: sandbox adapter signs sandboxed requests with a short-lived operator-bound token; audit records include only pseudo-identifiers when configured for residency/anonymization. See docs/security/privilege-caging.md for details.

Notes for reviewers: focus on decision cache invalidation semantics (services/authz/decision_cache.go) and audit pipeline privacy knobs (pkg/audit/fanout_sanitizer.go).

changelog_entry: Security: Add privilege-caging middleware to enforce temporal RBAC throttles and per-operator KMS consumption sandboxing (feature-flagged).
notes_for_ops: Enable 'privilege_caging' feature flag in staging first. Observe metrics: privilege_cage.allowed_count, privilege_cage.throttled_count, kms.sandbox.fallback_count. If fallback_count rises sharply, investigate KMS budgets for the affected operator or increase fallback pool capacity.
risk_assessment: Medium - introduces an enforcement path in the request stack and a new KMS adapter. Feature-flagged and can be turned to dry-run to mitigate risk.
